note: Every source this pack is built from, with the digest and size measured on 2026-10-10.
`evidence.quote` is the exact sentence the licence was read from, on `evidence.url`; a source
without one is not used, and the builder refuses bytes that do not match `sha256` and `bytes`.
The three Army PDFs and FEMA's guide are works of the U.S. Government, not subject to copyright
in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105(a)); each Army PDF also prints its own distribution
statement, which is the evidence quoted for it. FM 21-76 is served over http only, so its
integrity rests on the pinned digest rather than on the transport.
`vocabulary` is a source's own running-head tokens: the second opinion the margin band uses
when a page's furniture sits closer to the text block than the band. The ATP's `6HSWHPEHU` is
its cover date as that PDF's broken font extracts it, and it is furniture whichever letters
it carries. `runningTitle` is the one source whose text layer sits at an uneven height: FEMA's
guide prints `Are You Ready? <section>` on every page, and the line is furniture when nothing
but a few words follow the title.
`figures: "none"` means the source ships as text: FEMA's 2004 guide is a 204-page scan whose
text layer carries no caption for any of its images, so the pack takes its words and leaves
the pictures, which docs/packs/survival.md states.
For an HTML source, `bytes` and `sha256` are those of the page's own `<article>` element, which
is the part of the page the pack is made of. Measured on 2026-10-10: a federal page's whole
response can move between two fetches (FoodSafety.gov's did, its article element did not), so
pin the element rather than the envelope. The builder extracts the element, hashes it, and
refuses a mismatch exactly as it does for a PDF.
